posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 units in July, bringing its seven-month total to 216,322 vehicles, which accounts for only 39% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
To meet its full-year goal, the company must achieve an aggressive average of nearly 67,000 monthly deliveries for the remainder of the year, more than double its current pace.
The company's growth strategy hinges on the upcoming September launch of the Sky Nomad EREV series, which is priced to compete directly with Li Auto and Huawei-backed Aito models.

posts.title: Chengdu Auto Show opens next week with nearly 120 brands, 1,600 vehicles
posts.summary:
The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show, China's first A-level event of the second half, will feature 120 brands and 1,600 vehicles across 220,000 square meters.
Major manufacturers are using the event to debut key products, including BYD's D-segment luxury flagship sedan and Huawei's new Maextro V800 and V680 MPVs.
The show serves as a critical barometer for southwestern market demand and a strategic launchpad for automakers ahead of the industry's peak sales season.

posts.title: Hyundai's first Ioniq model for China to open pre-sales at Chengdu Auto Show
posts.summary:
The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Beijing Hyundai will open pre-sales for the Ioniq V, its first China-produced Ioniq model, at the Chengdu Auto Show with an official launch scheduled for September.
The mid-size electric sedan features 800-volt fast charging, a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8295 chip, and integrated AI models from Baidu and ByteDance.
Developed by Hyundai's China design center, the vehicle utilizes Momenta's L2+ smart driving solutions and is intended for both the domestic market and global export.

posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: Enterprise AI adoption is currently bottlenecked by legacy data infrastructure, which struggles to provide the real-time, cross-functional access required for autonomous agentic workflows.
A survey of 300 executives reveals that AI agents currently access only 45% of available enterprise data on average, with 'data laggards' restricted to 30% or less.
Organizations identified as 'data leaders' provide agents with access to over 70% of their data, directly correlating with higher ROI and more reliable autonomous decision-making.
With Gartner projecting that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, firms must modernize data architectures to avoid operational obsolescence.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to support linear drive optics in high-speed AI infrastructure.
Transitioning to linear optics allows for the removal of DSPs and retimers, which can reduce module power consumption by up to 50% and significantly lower thermal loads in dense AI racks.
The new PHY IP meets or exceeds OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for TX/RX performance, including metrics like jitter and eye-closure, ensuring interoperability within the ecosystem.
This technology enables DSP-less host-to-module connectivity, providing a scalable architectural path toward future 224G/448G interconnects and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO).
